Legend

US EPA Air Quality Index (AQI, PM2.5-based, bright Apple-style 0-500 slider): 0-50 Good, bright yellow-green deepening to vivid green → 51-100 Moderate vivid yellow → 101-150 Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups vivid orange → 151-200 Unhealthy vivid red → 201-300 Very Unhealthy bright purple → 301-500 Hazardous deep purple to crimson/burgundy. Same AQI always shows the same color. CAMS PM2.5 model analysis converted via EPA PM2.5 breakpoints — not station observations.

Near-surface fine-particulate (PM2.5) conditions from the CAMS atmospheric-composition analysis: a continuous field flagging wildfire-smoke intrusions, urban haze, and regional pollutant transport over the Great Lakes. Low values mark clean air; orange, red, and purple mark progressively degraded, unhealthy air. The underlying variable is CAMS PM2.5, converted to the US EPA Air Quality Index via EPA PM2.5 breakpoints and identified as modeled output (CAMS analysis), not station observations.

Air-quality science (atmospheric chemistry and public-health exposure assessment) tracks PM2.5, particles under 2.5 micrometers that penetrate deep into lungs. The US EPA Air Quality Index converts PM2.5 concentrations to health-based breakpoints (good, moderate, unhealthy for sensitive groups, unhealthy, very unhealthy, hazardous) on a fixed 0-500 scale. This layer shows the AQI computed from modeled CAMS concentration, not aerosol optical depth, and is labeled as model output rather than station observations.

Units: AQI index 0-500 (display; source ug/m3 PM2.5 as filed)
